clue.text: Keeps coppers supplied with books

parts.note: coppers are pennies, abbreviated P
to book a table or seat is to reserve it, so books means reserves

explanation.surface: Someone keeps the police force stocked with reading matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coppers' suggests police officers, but here it means copper coins: P is the abbreviation for pence.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep food or a custom is to maintain or save it, a direct verb synonym.

clue.text: Get better soldiers to provide protection

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a common crossword stand-in for soldiers
cover is shelter or protection

explanation.surface: An army unit is drafted in to shield a recovering patient.
explanation.definitionFit: To get better after illness is to regain health, the core sense of the verb.

clue.text: Source of cash for the Highlander? It depends on him!

definitions.text: Source of cash for the Highlander? It depends on him!

parts.words: Source of cash for the Highlander? It depends on him!
parts.note: the Scots kilt-wearer keeps his money in a pouch, and that pouch literally hangs from (depends on) his belt

explanation.surface: A Scotsman's wealth seems to rest entirely on his own efforts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Depends' is used in its old literal sense of 'hangs down from'. A sporran is the fur pouch worn at the front of a Highland kilt.
explanation.definitionFit: The pouch worn on a kilt serves as a Scotsman's purse, hanging from his waist.

clue.text: Daring or otherwise, here's the way to get around town

definitions.text: here's the way to get around town

indicators.note: otherwise means arranged differently, so the letters of the two words before are reworked

explanation.surface: Whether you are bold or not, this is the route that circles the town.
explanation.definitionFit: A bypass road circling a town centre lets traffic go round it rather than through.

clue.text: A girl is turning brown

indicators.note: turning tells us the girl's name followed by the word is runs backwards

parts.note: Anne is a girl's name
taken as written

explanation.surface: A young woman is becoming suntanned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses the whole run ANNEIS. The leading 'A' is just the article.
explanation.definitionFit: Sienna is an earthy pigment of yellowish or reddish brown, named after the Italian city.

clue.text: Housing an animal in unusually nice environs could be a bloomer

indicators.note: housing means lodging one thing within another
in places the animal inside the reworked letters
environs are surroundings, so the shuffled word forms the outside wrapping
unusually means the four letters of nice are put in an odd order

parts.note: an eland is a large African antelope

explanation.surface: Keeping a pet somewhere pleasant might turn out to be a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: The shuffle of NICE ('unusually') gives CINE, which goes round ELAND. 'Bloomer' looks like a mistake but means a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Celandine is a yellow-flowered plant, and a plant that flowers is fancifully a bloomer.

clue.text: After getting discharged, turn up for support of a kind

parts.note: fired means discharged, as a gun or an employee

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom, i.e. backwards

parts.note: a go is a turn in a game

explanation.surface: Having been sacked, someone shows up looking for help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses GO to OG. A firedog is an andiron, the metal stand holding logs in a fireplace.
explanation.definitionFit: An andiron holds burning logs off the hearth, so it is a kind of support.

clue.text: Feeling tiny scene should be made

indicators.note: the letters are to be made into something new, signalling rearrangement

explanation.surface: A small dramatic incident is meant to stir emotions.
explanation.definitionFit: Sentiency is the capacity to perceive and feel, a noun for awareness through the senses.

clue.text: Detail to make a little mite miserable

indicators.note: a little says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone sets out to make a tiny creature unhappy.
explanation.walkthrough: The hidden run is m(ITE MISE)rable.
explanation.definitionFit: To itemise is to list point by point, which is to set something out in detail.

clue.text: Bill's written an article about foreign nobility

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
c is short for circa, Latin for about
a count is a continental nobleman, the equivalent of an earl

explanation.surface: A piece of writing about European aristocrats is attributed to a man called Bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name but is an invoice.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradesman's invoice or statement of charges is called a bill.

clue.text: Eastern eccentric, close as can be

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so the letters of Eastern are jumbled

explanation.surface: An oddball from the East is very near.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of near, meaning the closest possible.

clue.text: In debt once again, and tense as a result

parts.note: over can mean again, as in start over
drawn describes a strained, tense face

explanation.surface: Someone is overspent again and anxious because of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank account taken below zero leaves its holder owing money to the bank.

clue.text: A bit depressed due to inflammation

parts.note: a whit is a tiny amount, as in not a whit
low means down or depressed

explanation.surface: Someone feels slightly down because of a swelling.
explanation.definitionFit: A whitlow is an infected swelling near a fingernail, a localised inflammation.

clue.text: Pass a portion which is quite liberal

parts.note: to hand something is to pass it
some means a portion or part

explanation.surface: Hand over a share of something generous.
explanation.definitionFit: A handsome sum or gift is a generous one, as in a handsome reward.

clue.text: A woman graduate will receive part

indicators.note: will receive means the graduate's letters take another word inside them

parts.note: BA is a Bachelor of Arts
to rend is to tear apart or part

explanation.surface: A female graduate is going to be given a role.
explanation.definitionFit: Brenda is a female first name.

clue.text: Viewing, being about to occupy

indicators.note: about means going round, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: taken as written
to hold a position or territory is to occupy it

explanation.surface: Watching while a person is set to take over.
explanation.definitionFit: Beholding is an old verb form meaning looking at or seeing.

clue.text: Assigns time for going round school, and sets off

indicators.note: going round means the first word encircles the school

parts.note: to date an event is to give it a time
Eton is the famous English public school

explanation.surface: Someone timetables a trip round a school and then departs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sets off' looks like 'departs' but means triggers an explosion.
explanation.definitionFit: To trigger a bomb or charge is to make it explode.

clue.text: Issue Number I with current backing

indicators.note: backing means moving in reverse, so the whole string of pieces is read backwards

parts.note: a tide is a current of water

explanation.surface: The first number of a publication comes with a reversing flow.
explanation.definitionFit: An issue of a newspaper or book is a single printing of it.

clue.text: Frequently concerning halfback keeping dry

indicators.note: keeping means holding something inside

parts.note: of can mean about or concerning
half is SEMI, and back reverses it
TT, teetotal, means not drinking alcohol

explanation.surface: A footballer playing at halfback often stays off the drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'halfback' splits into 'half' (SEMI) and 'back' (read backwards), giving IMES. 'keeping' puts TT inside OFIMES. A halfback is a midfield football or rugby position.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic adverb meaning often or many times.

clue.text: Police uniform?

parts.note: the law, meaning the police, plus a suit as an outfit, jokingly describes a legal action

explanation.surface: A question about what officers wear.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the clue as two nouns, 'the law' and 'suit', and the result is a court case.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal claim brought in court is an action at law.

clue.text: Felt a troublesome young beginner should show loyalty

indicators.note: troublesome means disordered, so the letters of felt a are shuffled
the beginner of young is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A tricky youngster ought to be faithful.
explanation.definitionFit: Fealty was the sworn allegiance a feudal vassal owed his lord.

clue.text: War that may be put across

indicators.note: may be put suggests the letters can be placed in another order

explanation.surface: A conflict that could be described as transverse.
explanation.definitionFit: Athwart is an adverb or preposition meaning from side to side or crosswise.

clue.text: Snarled when old Chinese went first

parts.note: the Tang was a Chinese dynasty of the 7th to 10th centuries
to lead is to go first, past tense led

explanation.surface: Someone growled when an old Chinese man was ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: A snarled rope or line is twisted into knots.

clue.text: Music man speaking to "X"

parts.note: an orator is a public speaker
X is the Roman numeral ten, written 10, which looks like the letters I and O

explanation.surface: A man talks to a mark, perhaps an unknown quantity.
explanation.walkthrough: Ten written in figures resembles IO.
explanation.definitionFit: An oratorio is a large-scale musical setting of a sacred text for voices and orchestra.

clue.text: This country is right, turning over grassland

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: turning over means the meadow word is flipped to read backwards

parts.note: a lea is a meadow or pasture

explanation.surface: A nation is correct to plough up its pastures.
explanation.definitionFit: A Middle Eastern nation on the Mediterranean coast.

clue.text: Punishment for making changes?

definitions.meaning: a beating with a thin stick or cane
swapping or altering one thing for another

explanation.definitionFit: Both a thrashing with a flexible rod and the act of exchanging one thing for another.

clue.text: The unhappy state of the French couple

parts.note: des is French for of the (plural)
a pair is a couple

explanation.surface: A French duo are in a sorry condition.
explanation.definitionFit: Hopelessness is the deepest kind of misery.

clue.text: Note the sailor in drink is easy to deal with

indicators.note: in puts the note and sailor inside the drink

parts.note: ale is beer
mi is a note of the sol-fa scale
AB is an able-bodied seaman

explanation.surface: A sailor with a drink in him is easygoing, it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: A friendly, good-natured person is easy company.

clue.text: Finding ways around good medico ingenuousness

indicators.note: around means the directions wrap the other pieces

parts.note: ways are compass directions, here north and east
A1 means first-rate, written as AI
a vet is an animal doctor

explanation.surface: Someone finds routes round a fine doctor's innocence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ways' gives two compass points, N and E, which go round AIVET.
explanation.definitionFit: Naivety is innocent simplicity, a lack of worldly guile.

clue.text: A certain weakness may make lads use it

indicators.note: may make says the letters can be formed into a new word

explanation.surface: Boys might exploit something feeble.
explanation.definitionFit: Lassitude is weariness or lack of energy, a kind of physical weakness.
